subject: Expansion pricing / additive workload tiering discussion
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@graniteai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@graniteai.com
Date: Wed, 05 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Expansion ask — two new products + cross-team onboarding (pricing/commit)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime performance looked great. We're close to a decision on the first phase, and two asks came up from the product and platform teams:

1) We want to onboard two additional product surfaces (customer support assistant + in-app summarization) on top of the pilot. Those will increase hosted API usage by ~45% on top of our pilot baseline.
2) We need clarity on how Redwood handles incremental commits vs. single lump-sum adds. Specifically: can we apply an additive commit for new workloads (separate from the pilot commit) and have those credits tiered for deeper discounts after a threshold?

High level constraints: a 6–9 month ramp for traffic, procurement prefers per-token pricing with committed monthly credits, and finance will require an SLA + simple SOW. Can you share a suggested structure (tier thresholds, incremental discounting, any conditions around burst/bucket usage)? Also attaching our internal usage projection and a short scope doc (attached).

Looking forward — can we get a written outline to present to procurement early next week?

Best,
Emma
Product Partnerships
Granite AI
[Attachment: GraniteAI_scope_and_usage_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@graniteai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion ask — two new products + cross-team onboarding (pricing/commit)

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear scope and the attachment. This is a common pattern and we can support an additive commit model that keeps the pilot separate while giving volume-based discounts for the additional workloads. High-level proposal follows; I'll loop in our pricing and finance leads (cc'd) for final sign-off.

Proposal (draft):
- Baseline: pilot commit remains unchanged.
- Additive commit for new workloads: set up a separate monthly committed credit (ADD_COMMIT) for the two products.
- Tiering (per-token rates applied to additive commit only):
  * Tier A: 0–50M tokens/month — list per-token rate (no discount)
  * Tier B: 50M–200M tokens/month — 10% discount to list
  * Tier C: 200M+ tokens/month — 18% discount to list
- Bursting: additive commit supports burst above the committed amount billed at on-demand list rate; we can enable a capped burst cap to avoid surprise bills.
- Top-ups: one-off top-ups apply pro-rata and inherit the current additive tier pricing when they push you into a higher tier.
- Ramp: propose a 6-month ramp with an opt-in 9-month extension if traffic grows slower than expected.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Agree on an initial additive commit number (we can model a couple of scenarios).
2) Sign a one-page SOW + commit appendix to attach to procurement.
3) Redwood to provide a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lists deliverables, dates, and points of contact.

I attached a compact pricing sheet with the incremental tiers and an example amortization across 6 months — this is intentionally draft so we can adjust thresholds.

If that sounds reasonable, I'll ask legal to prepare the SOW language and finance to validate the discount impact.

—Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-additive-pricing-v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Jul 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Expansion ask — two new products + cross-team onboarding (pricing/commit)

Looping in Lauren (rev ops) and Aditya (sales leadership) for quick approval on a bespoke additive slab for Granite. My comments inline:

- The proposed tiers look defensible. For strategic proof-of-scale accounts like Granite, I support a slightly steeper entry discount to accelerate adoption: make Tier B a 12% discount and Tier C a 20% discount, conditioned on a 12-month minimum commitment for the additive slab.
- We should offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent of 2 weeks of expected usage) to offset migration friction — payable as token credit, not dollar credit.
- Finance will want the SOW to include an annual true-up clause (to reconcile committed credits vs actual consumption) and a cap on retroactive credits.

Aditya / Lauren — can you confirm if the one-time onboarding credit and the 12-month minimum are acceptable? If yes, I will instruct legal to start drafting the SOW appendix and pass to procurement.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales Operations
